record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.context_brief: Fixed points on symplectic manifolds with χ=0
record.original_question: Let (M^{2n}, ω) be a compact symplectic manifold with Euler characteristic 0 that does not fiber over S¹. Must every symplectic diffeomorphism of M^{2n} that is homotopic to the identity have a fixed point? More strongly, must it have at least as many fixed points as the minimal number of zeros of any symplectic vector field on M^{2n}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture. Every symplectic diffeomorphism homotopic to the identity of (M2n; ω), where χ(M2n) = 0 and M2n does not fiber over S1, has a fixed point (in fact a number of fixed points ≥ minimal number of zeros of any symplectic vector-field).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a compact symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$ with vanishing Euler characteristic, $\chi(M^{2n})=0$, and assume that $M^{2n}$ does not fiber over the circle $S^1$. A symplectic vector field on $M$ is a vector field $X$ whose flow preserves $\omega$ (equivalently, $\iota_X\omega$ is closed). Let $N(M,\omega)$ denote the minimal number of zeros of any symplectic vector field on $(M,\omega)$.

Prove or disprove the following: every symplectic diffeomorphism $\varphi:M\to M$ that is homotopic to the identity has at least one fixed point; moreover, $\varphi$ has at least $N(M,\omega)$ fixed points.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a strengthening of the Arnold conjecture in the regime where the Euler characteristic vanishes (so Lefschetz theory gives no information) and where a topological obstruction to having no fixed points (fibering over $S^1$) is excluded. No proof or disproof of this specific conjecture appears in the literature; standard Floer-theoretic results address the Hamiltonian case but not general symplectic diffeomorphisms homotopic to the identity. The conjecture appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A symplectic fixed point theorem for CP^n
status_evidence.snippet: Arnold conjectured that any symplectic diffeomorphism homologous to identity has as many fixed points as a function has critical points; proved for CP^n.
status_evidence.claim: The Arnold-type conjectures are typically proven only in the Hamiltonian setting or for special manifolds, leaving the symplectic case with chi=0 generally open.

status_evidence.title: Topological Consequences (Lefschetz/Arnold)
status_evidence.snippet: A Hamiltonian map has at least one fixed point if the Euler characteristic does not vanish, by Lefschetz theory.
status_evidence.claim: When chi(M)=0, Lefschetz arguments do not yield fixed points, so the conjecture lies outside the scope of standard methods.
